entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Lucius Nonius Asprenas, a prominent scion of the Roman senatorial elite, navigated the complex political landscape of the early Roman Empire, serving as suffect consul in AD 6 under Augustus and later as proconsul of Asia. His career, spanning the transition from the Augustan Principate to the reign of Tiberius, exemplifies the enduring influence of established aristocratic families in shaping the administrative and social fabric of Rome during its imperial consolidation. Born into a family with direct ties to Emperor Augustus, Asprenas played a role in maintaining the delicate balance of power between the emperor and the Senate, reflecting the evolving nature of Roman governance in the first half of the first century CE.

Asprenas's political ascent began with his co-option into the consulship, a prestigious office, on July 1, AD 6, where he replaced Lucius Arruntius, serving alongside Marcus Lepidus. This appointment underscored his family's high standing and his personal suitability for such a crucial administrative post within the nascent imperial system. Following his consulship, he likely held various other administrative or military commands before being appointed proconsul of the wealthy province of Asia, a highly coveted and influential position that further solidified his standing among the Roman aristocracy.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Lucius Nonius Asprenas's career as a Roman senator and proconsul of Asia exemplifies the enduring power of aristocratic families within the early Roman Empire, contributing to the administrative stability of the Augustan and Tiberian eras. His lineage continued to produce consuls, illustrating the successful adaptation of the old elite to the new imperial system.
